nodes.name: Co-Fe PBA Nanocubes Coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: Solution A was prepared by mixing 0.6 mmol of Co(NO3)2 and 1.34 mmol of sodium citrate in 20 mL of DI water. Solution B, containing 0.4 mmol of K3[Fe(CN)6], was dissolved in 20 mL of DI water. Solution B was then added to solution A under stirring for 15 min to disperse the particles uniformly. The resulting mixed solution was aged for 24 h at room temperature. The final product was collected by centrifugation, washed three times with DI water and absolute ethanol, and dried at 70°C overnight.
nodes.source_text: 2.2.1. Synthesis of Co-Fe PBA Nanocubes. The Co-Fe PBA cubes were synthesized using a slight modification by the coprecipitation method... dried at 70°C overnight.

nodes.name: Co-Fe PBA Nanocages Etching
nodes.procedure: 60 mg of the PBA sample was mixed with 25 mL of DMF, followed by 15 min of sonication to obtain a homogeneous solution. The solution was then transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and set for a hydrothermal reaction of varying durations at 180°C. After cooling to room temperature, the products were collected by centrifugation, and the post-treatment was the same as above. The green catalyst obtained was labeled as PBA(cage).
nodes.source_text: 2.2.2. Synthesis of Co-Fe PBA Nanocages. The following procedure is used to modify the as-prepared PBA cubes: 60 mg of the PBA sample was mixed with 25 mL of DMF... The green catalyst obtained was labeled as PBA(cage).

nodes.name: PBA(cage)-WS2 Hydrothermal Growth
nodes.procedure: The main catalyst, PBA(cage)-WS2, was prepared by adding 20 mg of (NH4)2WS4 and 60 mg of PBA(cage) in 25 mL of DMF solution. It was then sonicated for 15 min and set for a hydrothermal reaction for 10 h at 180°C. The sample was labeled as PBA(cage)-WS2.
nodes.source_text: 2.2.3. Growing WS2 Nanoflowers on PBA(cage) Nanocages. The main catalyst, PBA(cage)-WS2, was prepared by adding 20 mg of (NH4)2WS4 and 60 mg of PBA(cage) in 25 mL of DMF solution...

nodes.name: PBA-WS2 Hydrothermal Growth
nodes.procedure: 20 mg of (NH4)2WS4 was added to 60 mg of the prepared PBA sample, mixed with 25 mL of DMF, followed by 15 min of sonication. The mixture was then transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and set for a 10 h hydrothermal reaction at 180°C. The sample was denoted as PBA-WS2.
nodes.source_text: 2.2.4. Growing WS2 Nanoflowers on PBA Nanocubes. As a control sample, WS2 nanoflowers were also grown directly on previously synthesized PBA cubes...

nodes.name: Bare WS2 Nanoflowers Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Bare WS2 nanoflowers were synthesized by mixing 25 mg of (NH4)2WS4 with 25 mL of DMF and setting it for the hydrothermal reaction under the same reaction conditions for 24 h. DMF was used as a solvent to reduce WVI to WIV. The post-treatment was performed similarly to obtain the final product labeled as WS2.
nodes.source_text: 2.2.5. Growing Bare WS2 Nanoflowers. Bare WS2 nanoflowers were synthesized by mixing 25 mg of (NH4)2WS4 with 25 mL of DMF...

nodes.name: PBA(cage)-S Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The PBA(cage)-S synthesis process was similar to the above method except for replacing (NH4)2WS4 with thioacetamide.
nodes.source_text: 2.2.3. Growing WS2 Nanoflowers on PBA(cage) Nanocages... The PBA(cage)-S synthesis process was similar to the above method except for replacing (NH4)2WS4 with thioacetamide.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms solid cube structure for PBA; diagonal hollow structure formation for PBA(cage); differentiates interior void structure of PBA(cage)-WS2 from non-etched catalysts; shows WS2 nanosheet coverage on PBA-WS2 cubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A solid cube structure formation was confirmed by the darker TEM image, as shown in Figure 1c... The diagonal hollow structure formation was seen from the TEM image (Figure 1f)... The TEM measurement clearly differentiated the interior structure of the PBA(cage)-WS2 from other nonetched catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows lattice fringes of WS2 nanoflowers on PBA(cage) with d-spacing of 0.628 nm corresponding to (002) plane, larger than standard WS2 (0.615 nm) due to DMF intercalation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM image (Figure 2c) shows the lattice fringes of the WS2 nanoflowers grown on PBA(cage). With a lattice d-spacing of 0.628 nm, these fringes matched the interplanar distance of the (002) plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image with EDX elemental mapping shows Co, Fe, and W evenly distributed across PBA(cage)-WS2 nanocages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The dark-field scanning TEM (STEM) image and associated energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping of PBA(cage)-WS2 showed that Co, Fe, and W are evenly distributed across the nanocages, as shown in Figure 2e.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS reveals Co/Fe molar ratio 3:2 for PBA cubes consistent with Co3[Fe(CN)6]2; PBA(cage) shows reduced Co/Fe ~1.33 indicating preferential Co migration during etching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX analysis of the PBA cubes revealed a Co/Fe molar ratio of 3:2, consistent with the expected value of the Co3[Fe(CN)6]2 template. In contrast, the cage composition had a slightly reduced Co/Fe ratio compared to the precursor's PBA cubes (Table S1), indicating the cobalt preference to migrate out of the cube.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-Fe PBA shows sharp peaks at 17.6°, 24.9°, 35.6°, 38.9°, 39.9°, 44.1°, 51.2°, 54.6°, 57.8° (fcc, JCPDS 75-0038); PBA(cage) and PBA(cage)-WS2 peaks slightly downshifted due to defect formation; WS2 (002) peak at 9.1° in hybrids due to DMF intercalation (vs 14° standard).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystallographic phases of the as-prepared catalysts were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectroscopy... The sharp XRD peak intensities of Co-Fe PBA at 17.6, 24.9, 35.6... Figure 3a.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms Co, Fe, W, S, O presence; Fe 2p1/2 and 2p3/2 BEs upshifted in PBA(cage) and PBA(cage)-WS2 vs PBA indicating higher electron affinity; W peaks upshifted in PBA(cage)-WS2 vs bare WS2 promoting OER catalysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The BE peaks of Fe 2p1/2 and 2p3/2 in PBA(cage) and PBA(cage)-WS2 were upshifted compared to that of PBA (Figure 4c), indicating a higher electron affinity that eases water oxidation... Similarly, the W peaks upshifted in PBA(cage)-WS2 compared to bare WS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines WS2 content in PBA(cage)-WS2 as ~12.5 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amount of WS2 in PBA(cage)-WS2 was determined using ICP-OES to be ~12.5 wt % of the entire amount of PBA.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR confirms coordination bonds (M–N≡C–M') in PBA framework and ammonia-containing species formation in etched PBA nanocages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra confirmed the coordination bonds within the PBA framework (M–N≡C–M') and the ammonia-containing species formation in the etched PBA nanocages (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates used to calculate double-layer capacitance Cdl values: PBA(cage)-WS2 = 1.44 mF cm⁻², PBA(cage) = 1.28 mF cm⁻², PBA-WS2 = 0.4 mF cm⁻², PBA = 0.02 mF cm⁻², WS2 = 0.05 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: using CV, we estimated the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) directly proportional to double-layer capacitance, Cdl... The Cdl values for PBA(cage)-WS2, PBA(cage), PBA-WS2, PBA, and free-standing WS2 were 1.44, 1.28, 0.4, 0.02, and 0.05 mF cm⁻², respectively.
